title: How many lines pass through one point, and through two points?
description: One dot and two dots are marked on two sheets of paper, and a ruler is laid on each. Turning the ruler about the single dot gives line after line, but a ruler touching both dots can lie in only one way. A second try through both dots lands on the first line.
teaching_notes: One idea: many lines pass through one point, but two points fix exactly one line. Watch for students who think that one point also gives only one line.

source: Rihan marked a point on a piece of paper. How many lines can he draw that pass through the point? Sheetal marked two points on a piece of paper. How many different lines can she draw that pass through both of the points?
video_script.why: The child sees that a ruler can turn about one point to give many lines, but that two points leave the ruler only one way to lie.
video_script.substitution: Lay a ruler on the paper and turn it about the marked point or points.
video_script.anchor: Ziva marks one point and Jia marks two points on a piece of paper, and a ruler lies on the paper
video_script.payoff_line: Ziva can draw many lines, and Jia can draw only one line

final_answer.value: Ziva: many lines. Jia: only one line
final_answer.spoken: Ziva can draw many lines, and Jia only one line

never_show: the count of lines through one point or two points before the answer beat
maths_rules: A ruler laid on one marked point can be turned about that point in endlessly many ways, and each way draws a different line through it.
A ruler that must touch two marked points can lie in only one way, so exactly one line passes through both points.
Check: a second line drawn through the same two points lands exactly on the first one.
Any two points determine a unique line, the same idea as stretching a line segment without any end.
video_script.design: One idea: one point gives many lines, two points give one line. A sheet with one dot and a sheet with two dots stay side by side, with a ruler on each. The method is the same way as the example in the book on the line.
